wdllGrading.item: 1. The read path cannot express a bare null, and the type enforces it
wdllGrading.evidence: readDocument returns Promise<SmartFileReadResult>, a discriminated union with no null and no undefined member. PROVEN rather than asserted by mutation probe M1: reintroducing `return null;` at the G-14 document-missing site produced `src/lib/smartFileStore.ts(461,5): error TS2322: Type 'null' is not assignable to type 'SmartFileReadResult'.` on real exit code 2. Reverted; typecheck back to exit 0.
wdllGrading.whyThisIsTheWholeRow: The G-14 rule lived in a doc comment a caller in another file never sees. M1 is the proof it is now the compiler.

wdllGrading.item: 2. Every absence carries its BASIS, and 'not found' is not a basis
wdllGrading.evidence: SmartFileAbsenceBasis.basis is a required non-empty string in the type and the zod schema (contract tests reject empty, missing, and absent-field cases). At the DATABASE, `basis` is NOT NULL plus CHECK (length(btrim(basis)) > 0), proven firing against a real engine: empty basis and whitespace-only basis both rejected with `violates check constraint smart_file_absence_determinations_basis_check`, a NULL basis rejected with 23502, while a real citation inserted successfully. The DB-level test inserts via RAW SQL, bypassing the store module entirely — which is the point: a guardrail that does not survive a clone is not a guardrail.

wdllGrading.item: 3. Only a POSITIVE determination produces a recorded absence; an empty lookup cannot
wdllGrading.evidence: absent-verified is produced ONLY by reading a smart_file_absence_determinations row; no code path constructs the verdict from a count. An entityId with no document row and no determination row returns `not-sought` and writes nothing. Integration probes: 'has NO determination row for a document nobody looked for' (count = 0), 'distinguishes NEVER-LOOKED from VERIFIED-ABSENT by row existence alone' (1 vs 0), and 'cannot record not-sought as a verdict' (rejected 23514 — a row saying 'we did nothing' would make the table lie about what a determination is).
wdllGrading.adversarialCheck: I attacked this directly by trying to construct a forging path: read path never synthesizes, recordAbsenceDetermination validates before writing, and the DB refuses an uncited row even from raw SQL. I could not construct one.

wdllGrading.item: 4. A held document with an unheld version is distinguished from an unheld document
wdllGrading.evidence: The two G-14 return-null sites now return different discriminants: `held-version-absent` (carrying title, accessPolicy, currentVersion and requestedVersion, so the caller learns what it CAN have) versus a document-level status. Contract tests assert the discriminants differ and that held-version-absent is NOT a verified absence.
wdllGrading.basis: Finding F-A2-CP1-2, found by reading smartFileStore.ts:307 and :322 at source rather than by reading the G-14 header, which named only the document-missing case.

wdllGrading.item: 5. The STALE indicator proven in BOTH directions on BOTH paths
wdllGrading.evidence: PRESENT path: the inherited G-14 both-directions property re-verified (23 baseline tests green before any change, still green after). ABSENCE path: 'FIRES on a determination backdated past the threshold' and 'stays SILENT on a recent determination' at the contract layer, plus DB-level age probes on a real stored determination in both directions. MUTATION-PROVEN: forcing isStale true => 3 failed / 44 passed, exit 1; forcing isStale false => 3 failed / 44 passed, exit 1. Both reverted, 47/47 green, and `git diff --stat` confirms 233 insertions / 0 deletions on the contract file so no mutation text survived.

wdllGrading.item: 6. The contract-promotion call is RECORDED, either way
wdllGrading.evidence: Recorded in `contractPromotionDecision` below, with the criterion, the verdict, the reasoning, and what promotion would require. The promotion itself was NOT performed, per the dispatch.

contractPromotionDecision.criterion: OPS-17 A-013 / operator ruling OR-A1: the Smart Files contract type is authored locally in legacy-design-tools with a NAMED promotion step to @empressaio/atom-contract, and the promotion criterion is 'when G-34 closes' — because typed absence was judged the last thing that reshapes the shape.
contractPromotionDecision.verdict: DO NOT PROMOTE YET. Recommend promoting after G-44, not at this row.
contractPromotionDecision.didG34ReshapeTheShape: YES, materially, exactly as OR-A1 predicted. The read path's return type changed from `SmartFileReadView | null` to a discriminated union; a new entity (the absence determination) joined the family; and the read contract gained five statuses, an absence-basis shape, and nullable freshness semantics. The criterion's premise — that G-34 reshapes the shape — was correct.
whyNotPromoteAnyway: The criterion asks whether the shape has STOPPED moving, and the honest evidence says it has not been tested yet. The store has ZERO production consumers (F-A2-CP1-3, re-verified at close: `grep -rn` for smart-file.contract / SmartFileReadResult / smartFileStore across the repo returns only the type's own two test files). A shape with no consumers has had no pressure applied to it. G-34 reshaped a type that nothing outside its own tests uses.

G-44 (corpus capture) is the first thing that will actually write documents and record real determinations, and it is the most likely source of the next shape change — specifically around what a determination needs to carry for a bulk sweep (batch attribution, per-source rather than per-document basis, and whether `not-sought` needs a queue representation). Promoting before that means the first real consumer forces a coordinated multi-repo migration, which is precisely the cost OR-A1 exists to avoid.

The cost of waiting is currently ZERO and the cost of promoting early is not. Right now a shape change is a single-file edit in one repo, as this row demonstrated. That asymmetry is the whole argument.

One genuine counter-argument, stated rather than hidden: OR-A1 warns that a 'named step' must not become a euphemism for never, and deferring a second time is exactly how that happens. That is why this verdict names a SPECIFIC next criterion below rather than deferring open-endedly.
contractPromotionDecision.recommendedNextCriterion: Promote when G-44 has captured a real Bastrop corpus AND recorded at least one real absence determination through recordAbsenceDetermination — i.e. when the shape has survived contact with actual documents rather than only with tests. If a second consumer needs the type before then, that forces promotion early and is a FINDING, not a violation (OR-A1's own rule), and it should be recorded as such rather than resolved by copying the file.

steps: This repo consumes a VENDORED TARBALL of the DEAD package name (@hauska/*) pinned at 1.6.0, not the published @empressaio/atom-contract at 1.22.0. Promotion therefore requires the cutover in backlog item 27 FIRST: move legacy-design-tools off the vendored tarball onto the published package. Publishing the type to a package this repo does not consume would leave the local copy authoritative and create the divergence OR-A1 is guarding against.
Author the type in the contract repo, publish a minor, then DELETE the local copy and import — never leave both. Two copies with no divergence test is finding A-CP1-F3 all over again.
The five-value AccessPolicy import already resolves against the vendored root export, so the contract dependency edge itself is not new work.

Decide where in the contract the family lives: `workspace/` already exists as a subpath export and is the closest neighbor, but Smart Files is a city-file family rather than a brokerage-workspace one, so a `smart-files/` subpath is likelier correct. That is a contract-repo decision, not this lane's.

findings.title: The fixture-drift gate is PG-VERSION-SENSITIVE, and would have produced a false green or a false red on any pg17+ build machine
findings.evidence: Local scratch cluster is PostgreSQL 18.3; CI runs pgvector/pgvector:pg14 (.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml:42). The drift check failed on exactly one line: pg18 emitted `CONSTRAINT smart_file_absence_determinat_determined_by_instrument_not_null NOT NULL` where the fixture had a bare `NOT NULL`. The checked-in fixture contains ZERO named-not-null constraints across 4229 lines, confirming capture on a pre-17 server.
findings.rootCause: PG17+ tracks NOT NULL as named catalog constraints, and pg_dump emits the name only when the auto-generated name was TRUNCATED at the 63-char identifier limit. The name was 67 characters. Every other column's name fit and stayed implicit — which is why exactly one line differed.
findings.whyItMatters: A lane on a modern local Postgres would either commit a fixture CI rejects, or hand-normalize the line and ship a fixture whose correctness rests on unverifiable reasoning about a server version it cannot run. The second is worse because it looks green.
findings.howItWasResolved: NOT by hand-tuning the fixture (which is what I did first, and then rejected). The column was renamed so no identifier can truncate on ANY version, removing the version dependency at the root. Post-rename the gate prints `Schema fixture matches live DB.` on pg18, and since nothing truncates, pg14 produces identical output.
findings.durableRecommendation: Backlog candidate: have check-fixture-drift.sh report the server version, so a future mismatch reports itself as version skew rather than as a schema error. Not fixed here — shared tooling, out of scope.

findings.title: In-scope deviation from CP1, recorded rather than absorbed: determined_by_instrument renamed to determined_by
findings.why: Solely to keep the longest auto-generated constraint identifier under Postgres's 63-char limit, eliminating F-A2-CP2-1 at the root. No semantic change: still NOT NULL, still check-constrained non-empty, still carries what did the determining.
findings.recordedBecause: CP1 declared the other name (mirroring the spine's verified_by_instrument). A design changed during the build is a deviation from the frozen record and gets stated even when the reason is mundane.
findings.verification: Post-rename: full lib build exit 0, api-server typecheck exit 0, 47/47 contract, 37/37 integration, drift gate exit 0. No references to the old name remain in source (only in generated lib/db/dist output).

findings.title: Parsing the entityId on the read path surfaced a state the CP1 taxonomy had not assigned
findings.what: A malformed entityId cannot be `not-sought`, because not-sought carries a jurisdictionFips and docSlug a malformed id cannot supply. It is reported as `lookup-failed` with a basis naming the malformation.
findings.whyItMatters: This is the reconstruction trap arriving from the other direction: a malformed id matches zero rows and, without this branch, would read as an honest not-sought — an absence claim derived from a broken request. Reporting a failed lookup says the true thing: no lookup happened.
findings.disposition: Handled without adding a sixth status, which I confirmed before adding one.
